paragraphs.source_en:
Methinks I see in my mind a noble and puissant Nation rousing herself like a strong
man after sleep, and shaking her invincible locks: Methinks I see her as an Eagle, muing
her mighty youth, and kindling her undazl’d eyes at the full midday beam; purging
and u­ nscaling her long abused sight at the fountain itself of heav’nly radiance; while
the whole noise of timorous and flocking birds, with those also that love the twilight,
flutter about, amaz’d at what she means (Complete Prose Works of John Milton (1959) ii
557–8; cp. MA (no. 231) note to l. 151)
See also Psalms ciii 5: ‘Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like
the eagle’s’.
 scale/Heaven] A classical pun in compliment to Hyperion; the name literally means ‘going
aloft’, Gk. ὑπέρ ἰών, hence ‘scaling Heaven’.
 eagle] Another favourite bird of Keats’s; see, e.g., Hyperion i 156–7, 182, ii 226, ‘Sleep and Poetry’
